page: Microsoft Azure D96nds_v6 is a general-purpose, network-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 Intel processor architecture, the configuration delivers 96 dedicated vCPUs alongside 384.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard general-purpose ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include discrete GPU hardware accelerators.

A notable hardware characteristic of the D96nds_v6 is its large integrated local storage capacity, offering 5669 GB on an NVMe solid-state drive. The host platform supports Premium Storage attachments and incorporates network optimizations for high-throughput operational demands. Public IPv4 addresses are not provided on a complimentary basis.

By pairing substantial multi-core compute with extensive local NVMe scratch storage, the instance achieves high resource density without requiring separate disk attachments for intermediate workloads. This hardware footprint offers qualitative efficiency for high-concurrency tasks requiring rapid local I/O. Optimal workloads include enterprise database deployments, large distributed cache layers, continuous integration pipelines, batch data transformations, and container host environments.
description: Microsoft Azure D96nds_v6 is a network-optimized general-purpose instance built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and powered by an x86_64 Intel architecture. The server is configured with 96 dedicated vCPUs and 384.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. A primary hardware capability is its 5669 GB local NVMe SSD storage array, providing high-capacity, low-latency disk space alongside Premium Storage compatibility. Operating without discrete GPUs, the instance is engineered to handle compute-dense and I/O-intensive workloads at scale. Its balanced core-to-memory ratio combined with extensive local NVMe storage provides high resource density and qualitative operational cost efficiency for large-scale deployments. The D96nds_v6 is suited for demanding workloads including transactional databases, distributed batch processing, ETL pipelines, and high-concurrency web application serving.
